justification: Changes how the DeepSeek reader sends a chunk (parallel instead of one after another) and one page range; what is read and returned is unchanged.

pre_impl.existing_data: none: the reader writes nothing; its output goes to the existing review queue
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: answers can arrive in any order; pool.map returns them in submission order
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: applies to the next DeepSeek read
pre_impl.external_source_error: OpenRouter rate limit: each piece keeps its own retry; up to 8 at once (AI_DEEPSEEK_PARALLEL)
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: a failed piece raises as before and the chapter read fails visibly

functions.name: ai_extractor._call_deepseek
functions.input: one chunk's PDF bytes and the brief
functions.output: the chunk's provisions in page order
functions.if_none: an empty piece is retried, then left to the page-coverage guard, as before

break_it.scenario: The first piece answers after the second
break_it.what_happens: rules would be stored out of page order with wrong pages
break_it.how: pool.map keeps submission order; each piece sets its pages from its own start

break_it.scenario: A page range past the end of the PDF
break_it.what_happens: the chapter is refused every batch
break_it.how: Ku-ring-gai 9C.16 corrected to 34-34, checked against the PDF (34 pages, 9C.16 on page 34)

break_it.scenario: Eight pieces at once hit an OpenRouter rate limit
break_it.what_happens: a piece raises and the chapter read fails
break_it.how: the failure is visible (READ FAILED, chapter stays needs_extraction for retry); AI_DEEPSEEK_PARALLEL lowers the width; a 12-page chunk has only 3 pieces, so 8 is never reached today

falsifiable_check.fails_when: parallel answers are joined out of page order
falsifiable_check.observed_red: none observed: the order test passes because pool.map preserves order; it would fail with as_completed
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Parramatta 2026-10-14: 3.6 pages a minute serial, 15 parallel (log line counts at 07:03 and 07:08)
